description_en: Central temple at the centre of a five-temples complex from the 14th-15th century.The monument is part of a five-temples complex located 1 km south and down the hill of Mānmā-Khām̐ḍācakra, the Kalikot district headquarters.The temple is situated at the centre of a quincux plan composed of fiveśikharatemples, locally known asdeval(or 'temple' in Sanskrit). The four other, smaller temples, are built one meter away from the central temple, facing its south, west, north and east facades. The four sides of the temple are each marked by two pillars supporting a small overhanging pediment. The monument has a single door, oriented to the south and framed by two pillars creating a reduced porch (Skt.ardhamaṇḍapa). The door has low-relief carvings of volutes and, on the lintel a represented of Gaṇeśa. Inside the sanctum are stone discs coming from a temple's pinnacle and a stoneśivaliṅga. The room is covered by a corbelled vault.The four pillars erected around the structure are richly carved by low-relief decorative motifs and representations of mediums (dhāmī) during oracular possessions (Andolfatto 2019). The tower (Skt.śikhara) above the sanctum has a pillared niche on each side. Each niche contains a large high-relief stone statue of a deity: Gaṇeśa (S), Durgā (W), two-handed unidentified (N), four-handed unidentified (E).Thepañcadevalaplan is mostly found in the districts of Dailekh, Achham and Kalikot, which correspond to the area controlled by the Rāskoṭi kings. This dynasty ruled between the end of the 14th century and the end of the 18th century. Furthermore, the construction ofśikharatemples in the Karnali region seems to have stopped before the 16th century, which narrows the dating of this type of plan down to the 14th-15th century.The site is mentioned inSharma 1972: 23, 25, 32;Sharma 2012: 198-199 andAndolfatto 2019: 201-214.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
